questions.question: Which Ethiopia SKU and pack size is the hero?
questions.why_it_matters: Price, pack art and label copy change by variant.

questions.question: Is the BOGO/B2G2 promotion approved for advertising, and what are its terms and expiry?
questions.why_it_matters: An unapproved offer is a commercial and legal risk.

questions.question: Which product claims may be used in advertising?
questions.why_it_matters: Origin and cup-count claims need substantiation and wording.

questions.question: Do we have cleared pack art, logo, typography and brand guidelines?
questions.why_it_matters: Pack and logo are exact commercial elements.

questions.question: What can the two benchmark Shorts actually establish?
questions.why_it_matters: Only preview frames and titles were accessible.

questions.question: What placement and safe-area rules apply?
questions.why_it_matters: Text and product must survive platform UI and crops.

questions.question: Who is the primary viewer and what do they need in ten seconds?
questions.why_it_matters: The hook, pace and CTA depend on the audience.

sources.title: Operator assumption: Reels and Shorts safe areas
sources.notes: Safe insets of top 220, bottom 320, left 60 and right 140 pixels are provisional and must be confirmed against current placement specs.

sources.title: SIL Open Font License 1.1
sources.notes: Inter is used as a placeholder brand font under the SIL OFL.

findings.observation: The Ethiopia product page lists 50 gm at Rs 499 and 100 gm at Rs 699, with a regular price of Rs 500 on the 50 gm variant.
findings.interpretation: The storefront headline 'from Rs 499' is not the price of every variant, so a single price card would be ambiguous.
findings.proposed_action: Do not put a price in the ready plan. Hold price until the hero size and the approved advertising price are confirmed.

findings.observation: The storefront announcement banner offers Buy 1 Get 1 Free or Buy 2 Get 2 Free with code BOGO or B2G2 and a free mug. No expiry or terms are visible in the captured text.
findings.interpretation: A live banner is evidence that an offer exists, not approval to advertise its terms or to imply an expiry.
findings.proposed_action: Keep promotion out of the ready plan. Hold the offer, code and expiry until the brand confirms advertising use.

findings.observation: The product page says Ethiopia is 'known as a Birthplace of Coffee', that 100 gm makes 50 cups, and describes a rich aroma with bold and fruity flavours.
findings.interpretation: These are brand-authored descriptions. They still need approved advertising wording and, for origin claims, legal review.
findings.proposed_action: Use only 'speciality instant coffee' with approved wording. Keep the birthplace and cup-count claims out of the ready copy.

findings.observation: The storefront exposes a product gallery and logo files on its CDN, but no brand kit, font, usage licence or advertising approval was supplied.
findings.interpretation: Public availability is not a licence. Pack art and logo are exact brand elements that must come from the brand.
findings.proposed_action: Request pack art, vector logo, font and usage terms. Hold brand assets as needs-approval until supplied.

findings.observation: The coffee reference preview frame shows a dark, high-contrast product composition with liquid, bold vertical type and a logo.
findings.interpretation: This supports a premium product-hero visual language, but only the preview frame was accessible.
findings.proposed_action: Adapt the visual principles, not the media. Plan a product-led hero with dark warm grade and bold type.

findings.observation: The character reference preview frame shows a bright 2D character, bold top caption and an Indian street setting.
findings.interpretation: This is a viable character-led route, but not the strongest route for a ten-second product ad with one hero SKU.
findings.proposed_action: Keep a character-led concept as the third option; do not use the reference footage.

findings.observation: Reels and Shorts are 9:16, sound-off by default, and overlay UI on the top, bottom and right edge.
findings.interpretation: Captions and product must stay inside a conservative safe area; the exact insets are provisional.
findings.proposed_action: Plan a four-shot story with burned-in captions and a safe area of top 220, bottom 320, left 60, right 140.

findings.observation: No brand font or typographic guideline was supplied in the brief or on the public storefront.
findings.interpretation: A placeholder font is acceptable for the plan, but not for final brand delivery.
findings.proposed_action: Use Inter under the SIL OFL for the plan and flag replacement when the brand kit arrives.

findings.observation: The storefront prices in INR, sells single-origin, filter, instant and gift coffee, and positions itself as specialty coffee.
findings.interpretation: The likely buyer values origin and craft more than discount, so the hook should lead with origin and product, not price.
findings.proposed_action: Lead with Ethiopia and the instant format; keep the CTA direct.

findings.observation: A ten-second product ad has roughly four usable beats: hook, reveal, payoff and brand close.
findings.interpretation: Four shots at 2s, 3s, 3s and 2s give each beat enough hold without rushing the product.
findings.proposed_action: Plan four shots over 250 frames at 25 fps.

findings.observation: No music track has been selected or licensed.
findings.interpretation: The cut needs a cleared bed; an unlicensed track cannot enter a render.
findings.proposed_action: Budget one library licence and keep a second track as a fallback.

findings.observation: The brief does not say whether narration is human or synthetic.
findings.interpretation: A human VO needs a release; synthetic narration needs an AI disclosure decision.
findings.proposed_action: Plan a recorded VO with a release and keep disclosed synthetic narration as the fallback.

synthesis: The product is real and the storefront gives usable raw material, but the commercial layer is not approved: the hero size, advertising price, offer terms, claims, pack art and logo all remain holds. The creative route can still be planned because the visual and audio work does not depend on those values. The two benchmark Shorts establish visual principles only; their video and audio were not inspected and their media cannot be reused. The plan therefore leads with origin and product craft, uses captions for sound-off viewing, and keeps price and promotion out of the ready cut until a named human approves them.
